features.description: ClaudeCLIExecutor + CodexCLIExecutor argv translation per role. Both executors read DispatchTask.permission_policy and emit role-appropriate CLI flags using the syntax probed and confirmed against the locally-installed CLIs on 2026-04-29. Claude implementer: `--permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools "Read Edit Write Bash"`. **Claude auditor: `--permission-mode dontAsk --allowedTools "Read"` — Read-only, no command execution.** Rationale: Claude has no OS-level sandbox available to the orchestrator; allowing any Bash matcher (even narrow ones) is not truly read-only because pytest writes caches, python is arbitrary code execution, and matcher semantics may not block shell redirection. For the first dogfood, file-content review only on the Claude side; command-running audit lives on Codex where `--sandbox read-only` enforces at the OS level. Codex implementer: `--ask-for-approval never --sandbox workspace-write` as global flags BEFORE `exec --json`. Codex auditor: `--ask-for-approval never --sandbox read-only` BEFORE exec --json. Includes a smoke that asserts `--permission-mode dontAsk` denies (rather than prompts) on out-of-allowlist Claude tool requests; if dontAsk prompts, F005b is BLOCKED.

features.description: Forbidden-flag guard. Three flags are explicitly forbidden, runtime-guarded, and tested: `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (Claude), `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` (Claude — the enabling flag for the bypass), `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (Codex). A guard function check_forbidden_flags(argv) in scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/executors/base.py raises ValueError if any forbidden flag is present. Both executors call the guard before subprocess.run as a final pre-dispatch assertion. Tests cover (a) the helper rejects each forbidden flag directly, and (b) no produced argv across all role combinations contains any forbidden flag.

Add a check_forbidden_flags(argv: list[str]) -> None helper that raises ValueError(f'forbidden flag in argv: {flag}') if any FORBIDDEN_FLAGS member is in argv
Wire the helper into ClaudeCLIExecutor.dispatch and CodexCLIExecutor.dispatch as a final pre-subprocess assertion
Add a direct unit test: check_forbidden_flags(['claude', '--dangerously-skip-permissions']) raises ValueError; same for the other two flags
Add a parameterized produced-argv test sweeping role ∈ {implementer, auditor, None} × executor ∈ {Claude, Codex} = 6 cases; assert NO forbidden flag appears in the produced argv for any combination

Both executors call the guard before subprocess.run (verified by a test that monkey-patches subprocess.run to record calls).

features.description: First-class no-hang invariant test for all four (executor, role) paths, with sentinel write/no-write assertions. Two test layers per the locked acceptance: (a) fake-CLI shim tests in the default pytest suite covering the argv-shape end-to-end for each (executor, role) combination, fast and version-independent — these assert the shim received the expected role flags AND wrote/didn't-write a sentinel file consistent with the role; (b) real-CLI integration tests gated by env var `JARVIS_RUN_REAL_CLI_TESTS=1` (NOT a global pytest config change), which actually invoke `claude -p` and `codex exec` with implementer AND auditor flags against minimal write/read tasks with timeout=15s. The auditor real-CLI tests additionally assert that an out-of-allowlist tool attempt exits with denial rather than TimeoutExpired AND no sentinel file was created. 'No timeout' alone is not sufficient — the success cases must show evidence the agent actually attempted tool use (sentinel file present), and the deny cases must show the file was NOT created.
steps: Add tests/fake-cli/{fake-claude,fake-codex} shell scripts that echo argv to stderr, parse role hint from argv, and write evidence/sentinel-<role>.txt in cwd ONLY when the role flags indicate write capability (implementer for both, NOT for either auditor)

Add test_executor_permission_smoke.py: invokes ClaudeCLIExecutor + CodexCLIExecutor with role ∈ {implementer, auditor} using fake-CLI binaries; 4 cases total. Each asserts dispatch returns success AND verifies sentinel presence: implementer cases assert sentinel-implementer.txt EXISTS; auditor cases assert sentinel-auditor.txt does NOT exist (the shim refused to write because role flags were Read-only).

Add test_executor_real_cli_no_hang.py gated by `os.environ.get('JARVIS_RUN_REAL_CLI_TESTS') == '1'` (skip otherwise) with 6 cases: (1) Claude implementer write task — assert no TimeoutExpired AND sentinel file written; (2) Claude auditor read task — assert no TimeoutExpired AND no file written AND response contains read content; (3) Claude auditor Edit-attempt — assert no TimeoutExpired AND target file NOT created AND response indicates denial; (4) Codex implementer write task — same as (1) with Codex; (5) Codex auditor read task — same as (2) with Codex; (6) Codex auditor write-attempt — same as (3) with Codex (sandbox-deny instead of dontAsk-deny).

Do NOT modify pyproject.toml or pytest config addopts. The slow tests use the env-var gate so default `pytest` runs them as no-ops without the env var, and CI can opt in selectively without changing global config.

Document in test docstrings: 'a real subprocess invocation must not block on a permission prompt AND must show sentinel write/no-write consistent with the role' is the regression criterion. Show the manual command: `JARVIS_RUN_REAL_CLI_TESTS=1 pytest scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/tests/test_executor_real_cli_no_hang.py`.
features.acceptance: (a) Fake-CLI shim test: 4 (executor, role) cases pass in default pytest suite, each <2s, and each verifies sentinel write (implementer) or no-write (auditor) — not just no-timeout. (b) Real-CLI no-hang test exists with 4 cases (gated by JARVIS_RUN_REAL_CLI_TESTS=1 env var per D014, NOT addopts); when run with the env var set and both CLIs installed, all 4 complete within 15s without TimeoutExpired AND each asserts sentinel write/no-write consistent with the role. (c) Default `pytest scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/tests/ -q` (without the env var) reports 222 tests passing + 4 real-CLI skipped cleanly. (d) pyproject.toml addopts unchanged. (e) Test file docstrings explicitly state both regression criteria (no-timeout AND sentinel-consistent).
